heading: INT. WAX MUSEUM - AFTER HOURS - NIGHT

units.text: INT. WAX MUSEUM - AFTER HOURS - NIGHT
A wax museum at midnight.
Rows of lifelike figures in period costume, glass eyes catching the exit light.
A velvet rope sags.
A faint scent of melting paraffin hangs in the dark.
INSPECTOR HOLLIS DRAKE, fifties, trench-coated, a pocket flashlight in his teeth, crouches by a figure of Napoleon.
DR. WILHELMINA VOSS, forties, the museum curator, stands over him with a clipboard.
CONSTABLE REUBEN OKAFOR-LEE, twenties, shifts his weight at the door, hand on his truncheon.
MADAME ODILE FERRIER, seventies, the sculptor, sits on a folding stool gripping a cane.
LORD ASHTON PEMBERTON, sixties, the patron, leans against a plinth, his cravat undone.
NURSE JOSEPHINE BELL, thirties, hovers at his shoulder with a medical bag.
When was this figure last moved?
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: Never. It's been bolted since 1962.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: Then who changed his hat?
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: I'm sorry?
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: He stands.
He lifts the bicorne from Napoleon's head.
Beneath it, the wax has been scored with a fine hairline crack, and in the crack, something glints.
Constable, gloves.
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: Here, sir.
units.name: REUBEN

units.text: He hands them over.
Drake slides a gloved finger into the crack, hooks the glint, and draws it out: a small brass key.
Well, there you are. A key. How delightful.
units.name: PEMBERTON

units.text: Ashton.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: What, Odile?
units.name: PEMBERTON

units.text: You promised.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Pemberton straightens.
Josephine's hand drifts to his sleeve.
He shakes it off.
Lord Pemberton, you've seen this key before.
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: I haven't.
units.name: PEMBERTON

units.text: You have a matching one in your waistcoat.
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: Pemberton's hand goes to his chest.
Odile bows her head.
Wilhelmina lowers her clipboard.
Inspector, what does the key open?
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: Dr. Voss, I believe you can tell me.
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: The cellar. Under the Chamber of Horrors.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: And what's in the cellar?
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: The first sculpture. The one Madame Ferrier never exhibited.
units.name: WILHELMINA

units.text: All eyes turn to Odile.
She sets down her cane.
She lifts her chin.
I made her so well, Inspector. So very well. Nobody could tell she wasn't alive.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Who was she?
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: My sister.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: Ma'am?
units.name: REUBEN

units.text: She sat for me on the last night of her life. I could not bear to let her go.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: You knew?
units.name: JOSEPHINE

units.text: I paid to keep it quiet.
units.name: PEMBERTON

units.text: Constable, escort Madame Ferrier and Lord Pemberton to the carriage. Nurse Bell, you will assist Dr. Voss with the cellar.
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: Yes, sir.
units.name: REUBEN

units.text: Inspector, this is the Commissioner. Have you concluded?
units.name: PHONE

units.text: Nearly, sir.
units.name: DRAKE

units.text: Drake pockets the key.
Odile rises with surprising grace and takes Reuben's arm.
At the door she stops, turns, and looks at the figures one last time.
They keep better than we do, you know.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: She exits.
The wax faces stare after her.
Drake switches off his flashlight and the museum goes dim.
